subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (2, 4) and (−1, k), and A² = O, then find the value of k.

steps.label: Find A² in terms of k
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiply row by column, keeping k as a letter. The top-left entry is 2(2) + 4(−1) = 0 already, which is a useful check that the setup is right.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply row by column keeping k as a letter. The top-left comes to 0 already — a useful check.

recall.must_convey: That A² is worked out by row-into-column multiplication with k kept as a letter, giving 8 + 4k in the top-right entry.
accept: multiply the matrix by itself keeping k as a letter so the top right entry is eight plus four k
find A squared in terms of k using row into column multiplication
square the matrix leaving k in it
k ni letter ga unchi A square kanukovali, eight plus four k vasthundi
the entries come out in terms of k

steps.why: Keeping k as a letter through the multiplication is what makes it solvable. Substituting a guess first would only test that guess.
common_mistakes: Squaring each entry instead of multiplying the matrices.
Substituting a value for k before multiplying.

steps.label: Set the entries to zero
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A² = O means EVERY entry is zero. The top-right entry gives k straight away; check that the same k also kills the others.
steps.memory_tip: A² = O means EVERY entry is zero. The top-right gives k; check the same k kills the others.
lines: A² = O means every entry is 0:

recall.must_convey: That A² = O forces every entry to zero, and that 8 + 4k = 0 gives k = −2 — which also makes the other entries zero.
accept: A squared equals O means every entry is zero so eight plus four k is zero and k is minus two
set the entries to zero and solve to get k equals minus two
the top right entry gives four k equals minus eight so k is minus two
anni entries zero kabatti eight plus four k zero, k equals minus two
k comes out as minus two and it works in the other entries too

steps.why: O is the zero matrix, so all four entries must vanish — not just one. Checking the others is what turns an answer into a correct answer.
common_mistakes: Solving only one entry and never checking the rest.
Reading A² = O as det A = 0.

insider_note: Multiply out A² symbolically and set EVERY entry to zero, not just one. The top-left is already 0 whatever k is; the other three all give k = −2, and that agreement is the check.
